messages.repo-problem-missing: That folder isn't there. Check its name in .local/games.json.
messages.repo-problem-not-a-repository: That folder has no history to read. Check its name in .local/games.json.
messages.repo-problem-git-missing: Git could not be started. Install Git and look again.
messages.repo-problem-git-failed: Git stopped with an error. Look again, or run git status in that folder to see why.
messages.source-body: Each date and message is read from that repository's own history, its changelogs and its open-work list. This page only reads; it never changes a repository or a game.
messages.legend-observed: Read from a file or a repository
messages.legend-worked: Worked out from what was read
messages.tools-source: Read from the tool kit's own list of commands.
messages.tools-browser: This is the browser preview, so the tools can't be reached. The desktop program reads them.
messages.reports-title: What do you want to know about { $game }?
messages.reports-browser: Reports run in the desktop program.
messages.reports-empty: No reports for { $game } yet. They appear here once the tools can read this game.
messages.reports-running-note: The first run can take a little while.
messages.chart-picture: Chart: { $title }. { $description } The numbers are in the table under it.
messages.chart-failed: This chart could not be drawn, so its numbers are shown below instead. Nothing was changed.
messages.chart-key: What the colours and lines mean
messages.failure-refused: This program doesn't run that report.
messages.failure-refused-next: It only runs reports that read and need nothing typed. Choose one from the list.
messages.failure-python-missing-next: Install Python 3.10 or newer, or set PHOBOS_COMPANION_PYTHON to the one you use, then try again.
messages.failure-kit-missing: The tool kit is not where this program expects it.
messages.failure-kit-missing-next: Run git submodule update --init in this program's folder, or set PHOBOS_COMPANION_KIT, then try again.
messages.failure-tool-failed: The tool kit started but stopped with an error.
messages.failure-tool-failed-next: Open the technical details below, and run the same command in a console to see more.
messages.failure-unreadable: The tool kit answered in a way this program doesn't understand.
messages.failure-unreadable-next: This program and its tool kit may not match. Run git submodule update in this program's folder.
messages.failure-list-unreadable: Your list of games has a mistake in it.
messages.failure-list-unreadable-next: Open .local/games.json in this program's folder and compare it with config/games.example.json. The technical details below name the problem.
messages.status-reading-only: Reads your games, saves and repositories. It changes only what you ask it to: your test verdicts, in its own folder; your installed mods and their textures, from the Mods page; and the central settings file, from the Settings page.
messages.atlas-reading: Reading your newest save and drawing its world…
messages.atlas-reading-note: The first time can take a minute while the save is indexed. Nothing is changed.
messages.atlas-browser: The atlas is drawn by the desktop program.
messages.atlas-none: There is no atlas for { $game } yet.
messages.atlas-picture: A globe of the world map: { $tiles } tiles and { $places } places. Turn it with the buttons beside it or the arrow keys, and press Enter to see the tile in the middle. The tables below list what it shows.
messages.atlas-pick-middle: See the tile in the middle
messages.atlas-failed: The globe could not be drawn on this computer, so it is left out. The tables below still list everything it would show. Nothing was changed.
messages.atlas-hint: Drag to turn and scroll to zoom, or use the buttons. Click a tile, or press Enter for the one in the middle, to see what is there.
messages.atlas-tile-none: Pick a tile on the globe, or a place in the list below.
messages.tests-lead: The in-game tests from the test list. A row the game has seen working comes first, but only you can say whether it looked right: press Passed or Failed, and add a note if you like.
messages.tests-browser: The test lists are read by the desktop program.
messages.tests-none: None of { $game }'s repositories keeps a test list yet.
messages.tests-shelf-seen-note: The game noted these working without an error. Did they look right?
messages.tests-shelf-waiting-note: Nothing has been seen of these yet. Try them when you're ready.
messages.tests-shelf-judged-note: Your verdicts, waiting to be written into the test list.
messages.tests-shelf-done-note: The test list already says passed or failed.
messages.tests-shelf-check-note: Notes came for these, but they don't count yet: their figures are off, they came out of order, or they're from before the row last changed.
messages.tests-shelf-unrowed-note: The game noted these, but no test row asks for them. Ask for a row, or say none is needed.
messages.tests-concern-off: { $part }: seen, but not with the figures the row expects. Last seen with { $saw }; it expects { $expects }.
messages.tests-concern-stale: { $part }: seen only on { $version }, before the row last changed.
messages.tests-unrowed-none: You said no row is needed.
messages.tests-decision-failed: { $key }: your word could not be recorded.
messages.tests-you-cleared: You took your verdict back on { $day }.
messages.tests-seen: The game saw this working on { $day }: { $detail } ({ $made }).
messages.tests-recorded-cleared: Row { $row }: your verdict was taken back.
messages.tests-record-failed: Row { $row }: your verdict could not be recorded.
messages.tests-how-written: Your verdicts, and your word on notes with no row, are kept in this program's own folder. Verdicts go into the test list the next time it is brought up to date (python scripts/test-pass.py apply --apply, in the repository); a row you ask for is made by the next session that edits the list.
messages.failure-write-failed: Your verdict could not be written.
messages.failure-write-failed-next: The technical details below name the file. Check the disk has room and nothing holds the file open, then try again.
messages.mods-lead: Before you play, this says whether anything needs building, installing or encoding. Each mod then shows what it has now beside what installing from the repository would bring: changelog entries, files, settings and things to look out for in play. A changelog says what changed, not that it works in game.
messages.mods-reading: Reading your installed mods and their backups…
messages.mods-browser: Installed mods are read by the desktop program.
messages.mods-none: None of { $game }'s repositories says where its mods are installed yet (config/installs.json).
messages.mods-commits-since:
{ $count ->
    [one] one commit has changed it since
   *[other] { $count } commits have changed it since
  }
messages.mods-uncommitted:
{ $count ->
    [one] one file has changes not yet committed
   *[other] { $count } files have changes not yet committed
  }
messages.mods-state-ahead: Installed copy has entries the repository lacks
messages.mods-state-differs: Each has entries the other lacks
messages.mods-saves-heading: What the changelog says about saves
messages.mods-gain:
{ $count ->
    [one] give you one entry
   *[other] give you { $count } entries
  }
messages.mods-lose:
{ $count ->
    [one] take away one entry
   *[other] take away { $count } entries
  }
messages.mods-no-difference: Nothing: the two changelogs hold the same entries.
messages.mods-backup-change: Going back to this takes away { $lose } changelog entries and gives { $gain }.
messages.mods-confirm-dedupe:
Remove { $count ->
    [one] the one repeated backup
   *[other] { $count } repeated backups
  } ({ $size })? Each repeats the backup before it: the same file for file, or only rebuilt from source code that had not changed. The oldest of each run is kept, so going back loses nothing, and each is compared again just before it goes. This cannot be undone.
messages.mods-working-dedupe:
Removing { $count ->
    [one] the repeated backup
   *[other] { $count } repeated backups
  }
messages.mods-repeats:
{ $count ->
    [one] One backup repeats
   *[other] { $count } backups repeat
  } the one before { $count ->
    [one] it
   *[other] them
  } ({ $size }). The oldest of each run would be kept.
messages.mods-same-identical: Repeats the backup of { $when } file for file
messages.mods-same-rebuilt: Repeats the backup of { $when }: only rebuilt, from source code that had not changed
messages.mods-confirm-backup: Copy the installed { $name } { $version } into your backups? This only reads the installed mod, so it's fine while { $game } runs.
messages.mods-confirm-restore: Go back to the { $name } backup from { $when } ({ $version })? The installed { $installed } becomes a backup first, and this backup stays. It takes away { $lose } and gives { $gain } changelog entries.
messages.mods-confirm-install: Build and install { $name } { $version } from the repository? The installed copy becomes a backup first. Building can take a few minutes.
messages.mods-confirm-saves: The changelog says something about saves for what you'd go back past. Read it above, and keep a copy of any save you care about.
messages.mods-confirm-uncommitted: The repository has { $count } files with changes not yet committed; installing now includes them.
messages.mods-working-restore: Going back to the backup of { $name }…
messages.mods-working-install: Building and installing { $name }. This can take a few minutes…
messages.mods-move-failed: The move for { $name } could not be made.
messages.mods-space: Backups use { $size }; { $free } free on their drive. Old backups are listed by python scripts/cleanup.py in the repository, and go only when you run it with --apply.
messages.mods-how: Nothing here deletes anything: going back keeps the backup, and the install it replaces becomes a new backup. The same answers come from python scripts/installs.py and python scripts/textures.py in the repository.
messages.mods-before-this: The newest backup from before the change you came from ({ $when }). Going back to it undoes that change and everything after it.
messages.mods-before-none: No backup of this mod is older than the change you came from ({ $when }), so there is nothing from before it to go back to.
messages.mods-backup-saves:
{ $count ->
    [one] One of them is about saves.
   *[other] { $count } of them are about saves.
  }
messages.mods-pre-running: { $game } is running. You can build and make backups now; installing, going back and encoding wait until it closes.
messages.mods-pre-textures-failed: The texture check could not run; see the technical details by pressing Read again.
messages.mods-pre-textures-stale:
{ $count ->
    [one] One mod would show old pictures
   *[other] { $count } mods would show old pictures
  }: its textures are older than its pictures. Encode them before you launch.
messages.mods-pre-textures-missing:
{ $count ->
    [one] One mod has
   *[other] { $count } mods have
  } pictures never encoded ({ $pictures } in all). They work, but the game starts more slowly and uses more memory.
messages.mods-pre-ready: Ready to play: every mod is built and installed, and every texture is up to date.
messages.mods-pre-ready-mods: Every mod is built and installed.
messages.mods-confirm-build: Build every project in the repository? It writes only inside the repository, so it's fine while the game runs.
messages.mods-working-build: Building every project. This can take a few minutes…
messages.mods-confirm-install-all:
Build and install { $count ->
    [one] one mod
   *[other] { $count } mods
  } from the repository ({ $names })? Each installed copy becomes a backup first. Building can take a few minutes.
messages.mods-confirm-all-saves: Some of them say something about saves; their cards list it. Keep a copy of any save you care about.
messages.mods-working-install-all: Building and installing everything that changed. This can take a few minutes…
messages.mods-confirm-encode:
Encode the textures of { $count ->
    [one] one mod
   *[other] { $count } mods
  } ({ $pictures } pictures: { $names }) with RimSort's own settings? This writes .dds files into their folders, Workshop ones included. It can take a few minutes.
messages.mods-working-encode:
Encoding the textures of { $count ->
    [one] one mod
   *[other] { $count } mods
  }…
messages.mods-textures-lead: A mod's encoded texture (.dds) is used instead of its picture (.png) whatever their dates, so an old one shows the old picture. Pictures never encoded are only slower to load.
messages.mods-textures-stale:
{ $count ->
    [one] one would show an old picture
   *[other] { $count } would show old pictures
  }
messages.mods-record-approximate: installed before install records began; about commit { $commit }
messages.mods-lose-nothing: Nothing in its changelog would be lost.
messages.mods-unlogged: Files differ, but the changelog lists nothing new: a change nobody has written up yet, or code still to be built.
messages.mods-files:
{ $count ->

  }
messages.mods-settings-unknown: Its settings changes could not be read this time.
messages.mods-look-out:
{ $count ->

  }
messages.mods-in-step: { $version } is installed, and installing again would change nothing.
messages.source-body-mods: Each mod is read three ways: as installed, in its repository and in its backups. What an install brings comes from each copy's changelog and files, the repository's settings and its test list. This page changes your installed mods and encodes textures, only when you press a button and, where it matters, confirm.
messages.activity-test-code: Finding the code that notes the test rows
messages.activity-entry-code: Reading the code behind an entry
messages.activity-as-it-stood: Reading a changelog as it stood
messages.activity-mod-settings: Reading the history of your mods' settings
messages.changes-lead: What each changelog says changed, newest first. Show the code opens the commit that wrote an entry, with every file it changed.
messages.changes-browser: Changelogs are read by the desktop program.
messages.changes-none: None of { $game }'s repositories keeps a changelog (a file named CHANGELOG.md), so there is nothing to list yet.
messages.changes-tests-waiting: In-game tests still waiting on this version:
messages.changes-older:
{ $count ->
    [one] One older version is
   *[other] { $count } older versions are
  } in { $path }.
messages.changes-how: The code behind an entry is the commit that first wrote it into its changelog, found with git. Nothing extra is written in a changelog for this to work.
messages.source-body-changes: Each changelog is read from its repository as it stands. The code behind an entry is the commit that first wrote the entry, and what that commit changed. This page only reads.
messages.code-reading: Finding the commit that wrote this entry…
messages.code-refused: The code behind this entry could not be found. { $reason }
messages.code-uncommitted: This entry is in no commit yet, so this is every change not yet committed. Files git hasn't been told of are not shown.

{ $count ->
    [one] The same commit wrote one other entry, so some of this code is that entry's.
   *[other] The same commit wrote { $count } other entries, so some of this code is theirs.
  } Git can't say which lines belong to which.
messages.code-totals:
{ $files ->
    [one] One file
   *[other] { $files } files
  } · { $additions } lines added · { $deletions } removed.
messages.code-left-out:
{ $count ->

  }
messages.code-no-files: This commit changed nothing but the changelog itself.
messages.code-mode-new: The code as it now stands
messages.code-binary: A picture, a sound or another file that isn't text, so there is nothing to show line by line.
messages.code-no-lines: No lines changed: the file was moved, or only its mode changed.
messages.code-truncated: This file's change is long: only its first { $lines } lines are shown.
messages.code-show-version: Show the code for this version
messages.code-show-for-run:

  }
messages.changes-several-commits: This version was written in { $count } commits; each group below has its own code.

  }
messages.source-body-gamefiles: From Steam's own records of the game and its Workshop items, and from the folders where the game keeps its saves and screenshots. Read only: nothing is changed or deleted.

messages.gamefiles-lead: What changed since you last played, your saves, your screenshots, and where the space goes. Nothing here is changed or deleted.
messages.gamefiles-reading: Reading the game's files and Steam's records…
messages.gamefiles-not-steam: Steam has no installed game called { $game }. If Steam knows it by another name, give its Steam app ID in this game's entry in the games list (steam_app_id).
messages.gamefiles-game-updated: Steam updated the game after that: build { $build }, { $when }.
messages.gamefiles-game-same: The game itself has not changed: build { $build }, last updated { $when }.

{ $count ->

   *[other] { $count } saves

messages.source-body-about: Read from the running program itself, the repository it was built from (its version, changelog and history) and the third-party notices. This page only reads.
messages.about-built: The version you are running. Built from commit { $commit } on { $when }.
messages.about-built-unknown: The version you are running. Which commit it was built from was not recorded.

messages.about-installer-how: Your records, settings and keyboard shortcuts are kept when you install over this version.
messages.about-installer-missing: Its installer has not been built yet: ask an agent session to build it.
messages.about-current: This is the newest version in the repository it was built from.

{ $count ->

messages.about-browser: This is the browser preview: the desktop program says which version it is.

messages.decisions-done: Decided: { $question } The next agent session acts on it.
messages.decisions-answered:
{ $count ->

  }
messages.claims-none: No agent session holds anything right now.
messages.claims-held-old: { $by }, for { $age }: old, perhaps a session that ended without letting go
messages.claims-how: Agent sessions sharing this computer hold a version number, a test row or a file here before using it, and let go once it is committed, so two never take the same one.

messages.source-body-makeup: From the repository's committed files and its git history. Nothing is changed.
messages.makeup-lead: Every committed file, by mod and kind: how big each part is, how it grew, where the work goes, how much is tested in game, and what players get.
messages.makeup-summary: { $files } committed files, { $lines } lines of text, { $size } on disk, at commit { $commit }.
messages.makeup-made-how: Each block is a mod or part, then its folders, then its files, sized by the measure chosen. Press a block to look inside; the path under the picture goes back.
messages.makeup-lines-note: Pictures and sounds have no lines, so they are left out here. Choose Size on disk to see them.
messages.makeup-made-picture: What { $game } is made of, measured in { $measure }: each mod or part, then its folders and files.

messages.makeup-mix-how: One bar a mod or part, split by kind, biggest at the top.

messages.makeup-growth-files: Growth is counted in lines: the history keeps no file counts.
messages.makeup-growth-reading: Reading the history, day by day…
messages.makeup-growth-picture: How it grew from { $first } to { $last }, one stacked band a kind.
messages.makeup-tested-how: Each mod's rows in the in-game test lists, by the versions they name: passed, seen working and waiting for your word, waiting, or failed.

messages.makeup-tested-picture: How much of each mod of { $game } is tested in game, by state.

messages.codemap-busiest-none: No code changed in the last { $days } days.
messages.codemap-busiest-missing: { $file } holds nothing the tools read as a class, method, Def or function.
messages.source-body-timeline: From git, back to each repository's first commit, and from this PC's history log, which the tools write as they install, go back, back up, build and encode.
messages.source-body-settings: From the tools' own list of what they read, each repository's own settings file and the central settings file.
messages.timeline-lead: Everything the changelogs record, back to each repository's first commit, and every install, go-back, backup, build and texture encoding on this PC since the tools began keeping them. Read it as it stood opens a changelog exactly as it was then.
messages.timeline-browser: The history is read by the desktop program.
messages.timeline-none: None of { $game }'s repositories has a changelog in git, so there is no history to show yet.
messages.timeline-no-log: Nothing has been installed, backed up, built or encoded for { $game } since the tools began keeping a record, so only what the repositories did shows here. Those will appear from the next one on.
messages.timeline-showing-log: What was done on this PC

messages.settings-title: Where the tools keep and find things
messages.settings-lead: Every folder and file the tools read, for every game, and where each value comes from. A change here holds for every repository and every game, unless a repository's own settings name another.
messages.settings-browser: Settings are read by the desktop program.
messages.settings-central-none: The central settings file will be { $path }, once a setting is changed here.
messages.settings-value-none: Not set: the tool that uses it looks in its usual place, or says it needs one.
messages.settings-missing: not on this PC yet; the tool makes a folder when it first needs one, or says what is missing
messages.settings-env-wins: An environment variable sets this, so a change here takes effect only where that variable is not set.

messages.settings-key: Its name in a settings file: { $key }
messages.settings-saved: Saved { $key } to the central settings file. The tools use it from their next run.
messages.settings-cleared: { $key } is out of the central settings file: it uses a repository's own value, or its default.
messages.settings-how: The first of these that names a value wins: a command's own option, an environment variable, the repository's own settings file, the central settings file, the default. Saving here writes only the central settings file.
messages.timeline-batch-went-back: { $count } mods taken back to an earlier version together
messages.timeline-batch-hint: Press a mod to read its changelog as it stood then.
messages.source-body-logs: From the game's own log of its last run, grouped by the tools and compared with the run before. Read only: nothing in the log or the game is changed.

Open one to see where in the code it happened: a step of its stack found in your repositories opens on the Code map, where its history shows the changes that touched it.
messages.logs-none: The tools cannot read { $game }'s log yet. RimWorld's was the first; other games' come when their tools can read their logs.

messages.logs-stack-title: Where it happened, nearest the fault first
messages.logs-outside: Not in this game's repositories: it is the game's or another mod's code, which the Code map only knows where your code calls it.

messages.source-body-memory: From Windows' own figures for the running game, every 5 seconds, and from .NET's runtime counters when you choose them; what happened comes from the game's log when the watch ends. Nothing in the game is paused or changed. Watches are kept in the tools' cache, outside your repositories.
messages.shortcut-memory-mark: Mark this moment in the running watch
messages.activity-memory-stop: Asking the memory watch to stop
messages.memory-title: How { $game }'s memory behaves while you play
messages.memory-lead: A watch follows what the game holds in memory every 5 seconds, without pausing it, and says whether it climbs steadily or in jumps. Mark what you do as you go, so the figures can be read against it.
messages.memory-browser: Memory watches run only in the desktop program.
messages.memory-none: The tools have no memory watch for { $game } yet. It needs a game that runs on .NET and a watch in the tool kit made for it.
messages.memory-gotcha-save: **Save your game first.** With .NET's figures, the watch attaches to the game once as it starts, which can make it stutter for a moment. Windows' figures only attaches nothing.
messages.memory-gotcha-marks: **Marks need this window in front.** Switch here from the game (Alt+Tab), press B, type a few words and press Enter. The moment is taken when you press B, not when you finish typing.
messages.memory-gotcha-restart: **A watch ends when the game closes.** After a restart, start a new one.
messages.memory-gotcha-measure: **Figures are measurements, not a test.** When a watch ends, its report says first what happened (the saves the log shows loaded, your marks): read that before the figures.
messages.memory-state-finishing: Finishing: reading in the counters and the log
messages.memory-live-left:
{ $minutes ->
    [0] Less than a minute left
    [one] One minute left
   *[other] { $minutes } minutes left
  }; started at { $started }.
messages.memory-tile-collector: Held by .NET (the game's and mods' code objects)
messages.memory-tiles-how: As at { $when }. Claimed is what Task Manager calls commit size. .NET's figures arrive as the runtime's counter tool writes them, which can be only when the watch ends.
messages.memory-mark-placeholder: What you are doing or about to do, such as reloading PG15
messages.memory-mark-how: Press B to start a mark from anywhere on this page. Or press one of these, which marks the moment at once:
messages.memory-mark-none-running: No watch is running, so there is nothing to mark. Start one first.
messages.memory-stop-how: Nothing is lost: the watch keeps what it saw and writes its report. Key: X.
messages.memory-stop-asked: Asked the watch to stop. Its report follows in a few seconds, once it has read in the counters and the log.
messages.memory-label-label: A few words to find it by later (optional)
messages.memory-confirm-question: Watch the game's memory for { $minutes } minutes now?
messages.memory-confirm-dotnet: **Is your game saved?** This attaches .NET's counter tool to the running game once, which can make it stutter for a moment. Nothing in the game is changed.
messages.memory-confirm-windows: This reads Windows' figures only: nothing attaches to the game, and nothing in it is changed. It cannot split memory into .NET's and the rest.
messages.memory-start-how: Asks before it starts. Key: T.
messages.memory-start-refused: The watch did not start, or stopped early: { $reason }
messages.memory-command-line: The same report from a console: { $line }
